GENERAL SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: GENERAL SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Milk souring
   D. Ice melting to water

2. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 37 °C

3. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Transport in Animals ● Components of the human circulatory system ● The heart: s.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human Reproduction? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Human Reproduction.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human Reproduction.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Reproduction.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human Reproduction.

   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Salts II ● Solubility of salts in water ● Factors affecting solubility of salts .

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating ? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Thin Lenses 3.2 Newton’s Laws of Motion 3.3 Uniform Circular Motion 3.4 Heating .

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.

   C. Guess results without recording observations on Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human nervous system ● Components of the nervous system in a mammal (Central Ner.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Mole 2.3 Hydrocarbons 3.0 Natural Physical Science 3.1 Thin Lenses 3.2 Newto? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Mole 2.3 Hydrocarbons 3.0 Natural Physical Science 3.1 Thin Lenses 3.2 Newto.

10. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gaseous Exchange in Human Beings ● Structure, functions and adaptations of the h? (1 mark)

12. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
